requirements.title: Driver Configuration and Constructor Validation
requirements.rationale: A streamlined configuration structure with strict validation ensures deterministic driver instantiation while avoiding legacy configuration sprawl.

criteria.action: define Config with Client, Provider, Model, Effort, System, Prefix, Tools, Policy, Guard, After, MaxTurns, MaxCostUSD, Timeout, Prune, and MaxTokens fields
criteria.contract: agentkit.Config defines all 15 fields with the expected types

setup: the agentkit Go package
check.pseudocode:
cfg := agentkit.Config{
    Client:     &anthropic.Client{},
    Provider:   faux.New(),
    Model:      "claude-3-5-sonnet",
    Effort:     agentkit.EffortHigh,
    System:     "system instruction",
    Prefix:     []core.Message{core.UserMessage("preamble")},
    Tools:      []core.Tool{toolA},
    Policy:     core.NewAllowAllPolicy(),
    Guard:      guardFunc,
    After:      afterFunc,
    MaxTurns:   10,
    MaxCostUSD: 1.5,
    Timeout:    30 * time.Second,
    Prune:      agentkit.PruneOptions{Threshold: 0.35, KeepTurns: 2},
    MaxTokens:  4096,
}
assert cfg.Model == "claude-3-5-sonnet"

criteria.condition: both cfg.Client and cfg.Provider are nil
criteria.action: reject construction with an error indicating that an Anthropic client or core provider must be provided
criteria.contract: returns nil *Agent and non-nil error

requirements.title: Eager Shell Tool Guard Enforcement
requirements.rationale: Eagerly checking for shell tools across direct and nested tool hierarchies prevents accidental unguarded command execution before runs start.

    Guard:    nil,

requirements.title: Consumer Execution Surface and Concurrency Control
requirements.rationale: Restricting the public surface to essential execution and inspection methods provides a clean consumer API and eliminates legacy steering and session complexity.

criteria.action: expose its public API consisting solely of Run, Stream, Messages, Usage, and ReachableTools methods
criteria.contract: the exported methods of *Agent consist solely of Run, Stream, Messages, Usage, and ReachableTools

setup: an initialized Agent instance

criteria.condition: a caller invokes Run(ctx, prompt)
criteria.action: execute the minimal driver loop to a stop condition, record turns to its transcript, and return a RunResult containing transcript messages, usage, turn count, and stop reason
criteria.contract: returns (core.RunResult, error)

fp := faux.New(

criteria.contract: returns (*core.EventStream, error)

setup: an Agent configured with a scripted multi-turn faux provider

fp := faux.New(faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonStop, faux.FauxText("streamed response")))

criteria.condition: Run or Stream is invoked while another Run or Stream execution is actively in flight on the same Agent instance
criteria.action: reject the call immediately with core.ErrBusy
criteria.contract: returns core.ErrBusy

setup: an Agent with an active in-flight execution
check.pseudocode:
gate := make(chan struct{})
fp := faux.New(faux.Turn{
    Blocks: []core.ContentBlock{core.TextBlock{Text: "waiting"}},
    Delay:  500 * time.Millisecond,
})
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{Provider: fp, Model: "claude-3-5-sonnet"})

go func() {
    _, _ = agent.Run(context.Background(), "run 1")
    close(gate)
}()
time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)

_, err := agent.Run(context.Background(), "run 2")
assert errors.Is(err, core.ErrBusy)
<-gate

criteria.action: for any concurrent invocation of Messages(), Usage(), or ReachableTools() while a run is executing, safely return a consistent view of the respective state without deadlocking or data races

requirements.title: Prompt Assembly and Cache Breakpoints
requirements.rationale: System prompt guidelines and four-point cache breakpoints maximize model prompt cache reuse across turns while keeping system instructions aligned with available tools.

criteria.condition: assembling the system prompt for a model request
criteria.action: combine cfg.System with active tool PromptGuidelines deduplicated in first-seen order using prompt.Build
criteria.contract: the assembled system prompt combines cfg.System with active tool PromptGuidelines deduplicated in first-seen order

setup: a Config with cfg.System and tools declaring prompt guidelines with duplicates

criteria.condition: constructing outbound messages for a model request
criteria.action: prepend cfg.Prefix messages before the initial user prompt and conversation history
criteria.contract: outbound messages sent to the provider prepend cfg.Prefix messages before the initial user prompt and conversation turns

setup: a Config with non-empty cfg.Prefix messages and a user prompt
check.pseudocode:
prefix := []core.Message{
    core.UserMessage("Preamble 1"),
    core.AssistantMessage{Content: core.Content{core.TextBlock{Text: "Acknowledged"}}},
}
fp := faux.New(faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonStop, faux.FauxText("done")))
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{
    Provider: fp,
    Model:    "claude-3-5-sonnet",
    Prefix:   prefix,
})
_, _ = agent.Run(context.Background(), "user question")

reqs := fp.Requests()
assert len(reqs) > 0
sent := reqs[0].Messages
assert sent[0].Equals(prefix[0])
assert sent[1].Equals(prefix[1])
assert sent[2].Role == core.RoleUser
assert strings.Contains(sent[2].Text(), "user question")

criteria.action: stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of the assembled system prompt
criteria.contract: the final content block of the system prompt carries an ephemeral cache control breakpoint; the final tool definition in the tool list carries an ephemeral cache control breakpoint; the final content block of cfg.Prefix carries an ephemeral cache control breakpoint; the final content block of the most recent user message carries an ephemeral cache control breakpoint

setup: an Agent with System, Tools, Prefix, and User messages

criteria.condition: the resolved tool list contains at least one tool and model requests are dispatched
criteria.action: stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final tool definition in the tool list

criteria.condition: cfg.Prefix contains one or more messages with content blocks and model requests are dispatched
criteria.action: stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of the prefix messages

criteria.condition: outbound user messages are prepared for a request
criteria.action: stamp an ephemeral cache control breakpoint on the final content block of the most recent user message

requirements.title: Outbound Context Pruning and Context Window Bounds
requirements.rationale: Outbound context pruning prevents model context overflows by aging out verbose tool results while preserving complete conversation history on durable transcripts.

criteria.action: define PruneOptions with Threshold float64 and KeepTurns int fields
criteria.contract: agentkit.PruneOptions defines Threshold as float64 and KeepTurns as int

setup: the agentkit package

criteria.condition: cfg.Prune.Threshold is greater than zero before issuing an outbound request and the ratio of estimated outbound tokens to the model context window retrieved via catalog.Lookup meets or exceeds cfg.Prune.Threshold
criteria.action: replace the body of tool results older than KeepTurns in the outbound view with a single elision notice stating the tool name and original byte length
criteria.contract: tool results from turns older than KeepTurns have content replaced by the elision notice stating tool name and byte count; tool results within the KeepTurns window remain unpruned

setup: an agent configured with KeepTurns=1 and Threshold=0.35, where estimated tokens reach 40% of context window

criteria.action: for any tool result pruned in the outbound view, preserve its ToolUseID pairing with the corresponding assistant ToolUseBlock
criteria.contract: its ToolUseID strictly matches the ID of the corresponding assistant ToolUseBlock in the preceding message

setup: a multi-turn conversation with varying numbers of tool calls and pruned turns

criteria.action: for any outbound pruning operation, leave the durable transcript returned by Messages() and RunResult.Messages intact and unmodified
criteria.contract: the durable transcript returned by Messages() and RunResult.Messages contains the original unelided tool result content intact

setup: a run undergoing context pruning in outbound requests

criteria.condition: estimated transcript tokens exceed the model context window capacity retrieved from catalog.Lookup after pruning
criteria.action: terminate the run immediately with RunStopError and return an error identifying the model and context window limit
criteria.contract: RunResult.StopReason is RunStopError and RunResult.Error names the model and context window limit

setup: a conversation whose estimated tokens exceed the catalog model context window capacity after pruning
check.pseudocode:
fp := faux.New(hugeTurnGeneratingMassiveContent)
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{
    Provider: fp,
    Model:    "claude-3-5-sonnet",
    Prune:    agentkit.PruneOptions{Threshold: 0.35, KeepTurns: 1},
})
res, err := agent.Run(context.Background(), "prompt")
assert res.StopReason == core.RunStopError
assert res.Error != nil
assert strings.Contains(res.Error.Error(), "claude-3-5-sonnet")
assert strings.Contains(res.Error.Error(), "context window")

requirements.title: Turn Continuation and Truncation Notice
requirements.rationale: Decoupling continuation from provider stop reasons and synthesizing fixed truncation notices prevents partial tool execution bugs while allowing models to recover.

criteria.action: determine turn continuation exclusively by evaluating whether the assistant message contains one or more ToolUseBlock elements, independent of StopReason
criteria.contract: the loop continues if and only if ToolUseBlock elements are present, regardless of StopReason

setup: assistant messages with various StopReason values (e.g. StopReasonStop with tool calls, or StopReasonLength with no tool calls)
check.pseudocode:
// Turn with StopReasonStop but containing ToolUseBlock -> continues
turnWithTools := faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonStop, faux.FauxToolCall("c1", "toolA", "{}"))
// Turn with StopReasonLength but containing no ToolUseBlock -> does not continue
turnWithoutTools := faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonLength, faux.FauxText("truncated text"))

fp := faux.New(turnWithTools, turnWithoutTools)
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{Provider: fp, Model: "claude-3-5-sonnet", Tools: []core.Tool{toolA}})
res, _ := agent.Run(context.Background(), "test continuation")
assert res.Turns == 2

criteria.condition: an assistant message contains one or more ToolUseBlock elements and its StopReason is StopReasonLength
criteria.action: skip handler execution for all tool calls in the batch and append a synthetic ToolResultMessage to each call stating that the call was not executed due to output token limits
criteria.contract: no tool handler functions in the batch are executed; each tool call receives the exact synthetic ToolResultMessage notice citing output token limit truncation; the synthetic results are appended to the transcript and the driver continues to the next turn without terminating

setup: an assistant message with ToolUseBlock and StopReasonLength
check.pseudocode:
var handlerCalled bool
tool := core.Tool{
    Name: "my_tool",
    Handler: func(ctx context.Context, args json.RawMessage) (core.ToolResult, error) {
        handlerCalled = true
        return core.ToolResult{Content: "done"}, nil
    },
}
fp := faux.New(
    faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonLength, faux.FauxToolCall("call_1", "my_tool", `{"partial":`)),
    faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonStop, faux.FauxText("finished")),
)
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{Provider: fp, Model: "claude-3-5-sonnet", Tools: []core.Tool{tool}})
res, err := agent.Run(context.Background(), "trigger")
assert err == nil
assert !handlerCalled

expectedNotice := "Tool call \"my_tool\" was not executed: the response hit the output token limit,\nso its arguments may be truncated. Re-issue the tool call with complete arguments."
tr := findToolResultInMessages(res.Messages, "call_1")
assert tr.Text == expectedNotice
assert res.Turns == 2

criteria.condition: synthetic truncation tool results are appended following a StopReasonLength response
criteria.action: continue to the next turn without terminating the run

requirements.title: Batch Tool Execution Pipeline
requirements.rationale: Four-phase batch execution guarantees deterministic guard evaluation, atomic abort decisions, concurrent tool execution without premature sibling cancellation, and ordered results.

criteria.condition: preparing a batch of tool calls in Phase 1
criteria.action: sequentially validate arguments using core.PrepareArguments and evaluate Config.Guard for each call on the loop goroutine, finalizing any blocked call or validation error immediately as an error result without invoking its handler
criteria.contract: core.PrepareArguments and Config.Guard run sequentially on the loop goroutine; invalid and blocked calls are finalized immediately as error results; their handlers are never invoked

setup: a batch of tool calls including an invalid argument call and a Guard-rejected call

criteria.condition: evaluating the Phase 2 abort decision before any handler starts and the run context is cancelled (ctx.Err() != nil)
criteria.action: mark all remaining unfinalized calls as aborted without executing any handlers
criteria.contract: all remaining unfinalized calls are marked as aborted without executing any handlers

setup: a batch of valid prepared tool calls where ctx.Err() != nil before Phase 3 handlers spawn

criteria.condition: evaluating the Phase 2 abort decision before handlers start and the run context is active (ctx.Err() == nil)
criteria.action: dispatch all remaining unfinalized calls to Phase 3 execution
criteria.contract: Phase 2 dispatches all unfinalized calls to Phase 3; handlers execute concurrently in separate goroutines joined by sync.WaitGroup without errgroup

setup: a batch of valid tool calls with an active context

criteria.condition: executing tool handlers in Phase 3 without Sequential tools
criteria.action: execute handler functions concurrently with one goroutine per call joined by a sync.WaitGroup without using errgroup

criteria.condition: executing tool handlers in Phase 3 and at least one tool in the batch is marked Sequential
criteria.action: execute handlers sequentially in call order
criteria.contract: handlers execute sequentially in assistant call order

setup: a batch of tool calls containing at least one tool marked Sequential

criteria.condition: finalizing tool execution in Phase 4
criteria.action: evaluate Config.After and emit completion events serialized under a batch-scoped mutex while assigning results by original slot index to preserve assistant call order
criteria.contract: Config.After and event emission are serialized under a batch-scoped mutex; results are placed by original slot index to preserve assistant call order

setup: concurrent handlers finishing in arbitrary order

requirements.title: Batch Tool Termination Voting
requirements.rationale: Tool-initiated termination allows tools to signal mission completion while ensuring batches always finish executing cleanly and blocked calls do not trigger termination.

criteria.condition: any executed tool handler in a batch returns a result with Terminate set to true and the entire batch completes execution
criteria.action: terminate the run with RunStopToolTerminate
criteria.contract: RunResult.StopReason is RunStopToolTerminate

setup: a batch of parallel tool calls where tool A returns Terminate: true and tool B is still running

criteria.condition: an executed tool votes Terminate true in a parallel batch and sibling tool calls are concurrently executing in the same batch
criteria.action: await completion of all sibling handlers before terminating the run

criteria.condition: a tool call is blocked by Config.Guard or fails argument validation during Phase 1
criteria.action: record an error result without setting a termination vote
criteria.contract: the blocked call does not trigger RunStopToolTerminate

setup: a tool with Terminate capability whose call is blocked by Guard in Phase 1

requirements.title: Nested Tool Execution Pipeline
requirements.rationale: The nested caller pipeline enables tools like Starlark code mode to execute child tools safely with bound reachability, parent attribution, and error introspection.

criteria.condition: executing a tool that declares ReachableTools
criteria.action: attach a core.NestedCaller configured with the tool's resolved reachable set to the handler's execution context
criteria.contract: a core.NestedCaller configured with the tool's resolved reachable set is attached to the handler's execution context

setup: a wrapper tool declaring ReachableTools=['childA', 'childB']

criteria.condition: a nested call attempts to invoke a tool outside the wrapper's resolved reachable set
criteria.action: return an error result indicating that the tool is unreachable
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with IsError true

setup: a wrapper executing with ReachableTools=['childA']
check.pseudocode:
wrapper := core.Tool{
    Name: "wrapper",
    ReachableTools: []string{"childA"},
    Handler: func(ctx context.Context, args json.RawMessage) (core.ToolResult, error) {
        caller := core.NestedCallerFromContext(ctx)
        results, err := caller.Call(ctx, []core.ToolCall{{ID: "nc1", Name: "forbiddenTool"}})
        assert err == nil
        assert len(results) == 1
        assert results[0].IsError
        assert strings.Contains(results[0].Content, "unreachable")
        return core.ToolResult{Content: "done"}, nil
    },
}
executeWrapper(wrapper)

criteria.condition: a nested call is executed through NestedCaller.Call
criteria.action: emit execution events populated with ParentToolUseID matching the parent tool call identifier
criteria.contract: emitted execution events carry ParentToolUseID matching the parent tool call identifier

setup: a wrapper tool execution with ID 'parent_call_1' invoking child tool 'childA'

criteria.action: return an error ToolResult value with a nil Go error to allow wrapper scripts to process the rejection
criteria.contract: returns ([]core.ToolResult, nil) where the result element has IsError true

setup: a wrapper making a nested call intercepted by BeforeToolCall that rejects the call

criteria.condition: an interceptor votes to terminate during a nested call and subsequent calls are attempted through the nested caller
criteria.action: reject subsequent calls with core.ErrTerminated and propagate the termination vote to the parent wrapper result
criteria.contract: returns (nil, core.ErrTerminated)

execution_paths.title: Multi-turn prompt execution with concurrent tool batch

steps.action: invokes agent.Run with a user prompt
assembles the prompt with guidelines and prefix cache breakpoints and sends the request to the provider
returns an assistant message with parallel tool calls
prepares calls sequentially, executes handlers concurrently via sync.WaitGroup, and serializes results into slot order
returns a final assistant message with end turn stop reason
returns a RunResult containing transcript messages, usage, and RunStopEndTurn

end_state: the driver executes turns, prepares calls, runs handlers concurrently via sync.WaitGroup, orders results by slot index, and terminates with RunStopEndTurn
smoke.pseudocode:
toolA := core.Tool{Name: "toolA", Handler: func(ctx context.Context, args json.RawMessage) (core.ToolResult, error) { return core.ToolResult{Content: "resA"}, nil }}

)
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{Provider: fp, Model: "claude-3-5-sonnet", Tools: []core.Tool{toolA, toolB}})

assert res.Turns == 2

execution_paths.title: Outbound context pruning under token threshold pressure

steps.action: configures an agent with PruneOptions and executes a long multi-turn workflow
estimates outbound tokens before request and detects token count exceeding the pruning threshold
replaces old tool result bodies in the outbound view with elision notices while keeping durable transcript messages intact
receives the pruned request and returns the next assistant turn successfully

setup: an Agent initialized with PruneOptions(Threshold=0.35, KeepTurns=1) and a multi-turn scripted faux provider
end_state: outbound view elides old tool results with elision notice, provider receives pruned request, and durable Messages() transcript remains intact
smoke.pseudocode:
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{
    Provider: fpMultiTurnLargeResults,
    Model:    "claude-3-5-sonnet",
    Prune:    agentkit.PruneOptions{Threshold: 0.35, KeepTurns: 1},
    Tools:    []core.Tool{toolA},
})
res, err := agent.Run(context.Background(), "start multi-turn pruning")
assert err == nil
outboundReq := fpMultiTurnLargeResults.LastRequest()
outboundResult := findToolResultInMessages(outboundReq.Messages, "c1")
assert strings.Contains(outboundResult.Text, "[result of toolA")
assert strings.Contains(outboundResult.Text, "elided; call again if needed]")
// Durable transcript intact
assert !strings.Contains(agent.Messages().Text(), "elided; call again if needed]")

execution_paths.title: Synthetic truncation recovery on max_tokens response

steps.action: invokes agent.Run with a prompt requiring structured tool execution
returns an assistant message containing tool calls with stop reason max_tokens (StopReasonLength)
bypasses tool handler execution, appends synthetic truncated tool result notices to transcript, and continues to the next turn
receives complete tool call re-issue and returns the final answer
completes the run with RunStopEndTurn

setup: an Agent configured with real loop and faux provider returning ToolUseBlock with StopReasonLength followed by complete response
end_state: tool handlers are bypassed, synthetic truncation notices are recorded, and the run continues to the next turn completing with RunStopEndTurn
smoke.pseudocode:
var executed bool
tool := core.Tool{Name: "my_tool", Handler: func(ctx context.Context, args json.RawMessage) (core.ToolResult, error) { executed = true; return core.ToolResult{}, nil }}
fp := faux.New(
    faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonLength, faux.FauxToolCall("c1", "my_tool", `{"partial":`)),
    faux.FauxAssistantMessage(core.StopReasonStop, faux.FauxText("reissued and finished")),
)
agent, _ := agentkit.New(agentkit.Config{Provider: fp, Model: "claude-3-5-sonnet", Tools: []core.Tool{tool}})
res, err := agent.Run(context.Background(), "run recovery")
assert err == nil
assert !executed
assert res.StopReason == core.RunStopEndTurn
assert strings.Contains(res.Messages[1].Content[0].(core.ToolResultBlock).Text, "was not executed: the response hit the output token limit")
